stanzas.loss_note: The translation adds the word 'wrath' to rhyme with 'path', which is not present in the original Hindi text ('lagan' means dedication/resolve).

metaphor_spans.abstract_meaning: The speaker will continuously struggle against and overcome life's obstacles and hardships.

translation_loss.what_was_lost: The translation introduces the word 'wrath' to force a rhyme with 'path', which is absent in the original Hindi text. The original 'lagan' means dedication, devotion, or relentless resolve, carrying no connotation of anger or wrath.

stanzas.loss_note: The translation of line 8 ('And every challenge defies') slightly alters the active grammatical subject of the original Hindi, where the inner lamp/light ('deep') is what will clash with or confront every difficulty.

In the original, the inner light ('deep') is the active force that will clash with or confront every difficulty, whereas the translation makes 'challenge' the active subject that defies.

original_poem:
ना हार मानूँगा,  
चाहे राहें हों कठिन।  
लहरों से लड़ता रहूँगा,  
मुझमें है अनथक लगन।

अगर अंधेरा है घना,  
तो क्या हुआ, सुबह आएगी।  
मेरे भीतर का दीप जलेगा,  
हर मुश्किल से टकराएगी।

जीत का सपना आँखों में,  
मैं अपने पथ पर चलूँगा।  
ना हार मानूँगा,  
हर मुश्किल को मसलूँगा।
translated_poem:
I will not give up,  
No matter how hard the path.  
I’ll keep fighting the waves,  
With relentless resolve, my wrath.

If the darkness is deep,  
So what? Dawn will rise.  
The light within me will burn,  
And every challenge defies.

With victory’s dream in my eyes,  
I’ll walk on my way.  
I will not give up,  
Crushing each hurdle today.
